- The **12 agent-harness primitives**: permissions, approvals, persistence, tool pools, budgets, and audit trails.

content.text: I’m ordering the work around trust first: close approval and TypeSafe validation gaps, fix shared UI behavior, then strengthen recovery, budgets, and observability. The plan gives each unit specific files and acceptance checks, and covers all 12 harness primitives without treating existing implementations as proven.

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /tmp/indii-primitives-improvement-plan-2026-10-29.md
+# indii primitives: review and improvement plan
+
+Date: 2026-10-29. Mode: PLAN / `/better` AUDIT. Implementation has not started.
+
+## Objective and scope
+
+Make the existing primitives safer, more predictable, accessible, recoverable, and observable while preserving public contracts. Cover all 12 agent-harness primitives, shared UI/layout/loading primitives and both motion primitives, and TypeSafe Choice/Score/Noul across renderer and server consumers. Improve material behavior; avoid style churn, a new design system, a generic agent-role framework, or new autonomous product features.
+
+The repository has no `.agent/workflows/plan.md`. This plan follows the planning skill, `.agent/workflows/better.md`, the harness-architect reference, and the TypeSafe skill. Source inspection and official TypeSafe documentation informed the findings. No tests, live inference, browser journeys, or production checks were run.
+
+## Working-state boundary
+
+Observed checkout: `codex/near-loop-jev-architecture`, with existing tracked and untracked work. This includes `typesafeJudgments.ts` and its tests, ProactiveService, Firebase index exports, and new durablePulseFlywheel, creativeHillClimber, and onCallIncidentAgent files. Findings in those new files describe uncommitted work, not verified mainline behavior.
+
+Preserve that checkout. Before implementation, coordinate ownership of overlapping work, inspect current `origin/main`, and reconcile the intended patches without discarding changes, merging a stale branch, or switching a dirty checkout. Follow `.agent/workflows/branch-safety.md`: delivery is on synchronized `main` unless the user explicitly chooses a branch workflow. Do not assume this plan authorizes continued implementation on the current branch.
+
+Each unit below is a bounded delivery cycle: one coherent locally validated commit to `origin/main` via `git push origin HEAD:main`, inspect CI for that exact SHA, fix only logged failures, and stop that cycle when green. No independent `/better` commits. No merge or deployment is part of this plan.
+
+## Confirmed findings to address first
+
+| Priority | Finding and consequence | Evidence |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| P1 | BaseAgent intentionally skips the unknown-tool fail-closed metadata resolver. Agent-local functions without registry entries can dispatch without the metadata approval gate. Classify the actual custom-tool inventory before enabling strict enforcement. | `packages/renderer/src/services/agent/BaseAgent.ts:1548-1556,1598-1604` |
+| P1 | Missing/malformed tax Noul defaults to deductible; absent Choice confidence defaults to 1.0. ReceiptOCRService consumes this result. | `packages/renderer/src/config/typesafeJudgments.ts:805-831`; `services/finance/ReceiptOCRService.ts:79-91` |
+| P1 | Modal Escape is skipped while typing; handlers do not consume the event, so stacked dialogs can all close. PromptDialog focuses an input immediately. | `components/ui/Modal.tsx:43-49`; `services/keyboard/GlobalKeyboardOrchestrator.ts:102-132`; `components/ui/PromptDialog.tsx:31-42` |
+| P1 | Button with `asChild` advertises disabled/loading through ARIA but does not prevent child activation. | `components/ui/button.tsx:39-50` |
+| P2 | TabsTrigger spreads caller props after its internal onClick, allowing the caller handler to replace selection. All triggers remain in the Tab order. | `components/ui/tabs.tsx:99-129` |
+| P2 | FormField overwrites the child's existing description references and validation state. | `components/ui/FormField.tsx:27-39` |
+| P2 | Progress consumes `value` without passing it to Radix Root; the drawn progress and accessible value can disagree. Its visual math assumes max=100. | `components/ui/progress.tsx:8-24` |
+| P2 | TypeSafe transport clears its timeout before consuming the response body, declares but does not enforce the state-size limit, and ignores the optional per-request model. | `packages/firebase/src/functions/intelligence/typesafeClient.ts:96-164` |
+| P2 | Uncommitted on-call confidence is highest at maximum Noul ambiguity: `1 - abs(0.5-p)` is 1 at p=.5 and .5 at endpoints. | `packages/firebase/src/functions/security/onCallIncidentAgent.ts:369` |
+| P2 | Uncommitted hillclimber accepts finite out-of-range probabilities and requests a next-step Choice that it never uses to choose the next action. | `packages/firebase/src/functions/creative/creativeHillClimber.ts:251-291` |
+| P2 | Tool events flatten structured fields into text; audit writes are best-effort; per-call token ceiling does not establish a cumulative execution budget. | `governance/AgentEventBus.ts:54-67`; `BaseAgent.ts:1248-1265,1665-1691` |
+
+Renderer paths in this document are relative to `packages/renderer/src/` unless fully qualified.
+
+## Unit 1 — Explicit tool authority and approval safety
+
+Files: `services/agent/BaseAgent.ts`, `ToolRiskRegistry.ts`, `tools/index.ts`, `governance/ToolPoolAssembler.ts`, `governance/ToolApprovalService.ts`, relevant agent declarations and focused existing tests. Inspect server/main enforcement before choosing changes there.
+
+1. Inventory declarations, implementation maps, authorizedTools, global risk entries, and actual dispatch paths, including custom functions and A2A. Record missing metadata and contradictory classifications.
+2. Reuse one explicit metadata resolver at listing and execution. Add reviewed metadata for legitimate custom functions. Refuse execution of genuinely unclassified functions; do not classify every unknown function as harmless to avoid migration work.
+3. Preserve read-only, conversation-mode, domain, and computer-control opt-in restrictions. A model-visible filtered pool is not an authorization boundary; enforce authority again at dispatch and the relevant server/main boundary.
+4. Verify approved calls retain owner, agent, original arguments, and stable call identity. Examine concurrent approval, crash after claim, crash after side effect, denial, cancellation, and stale-state behavior. Distinguish recorded approval from execution receipts; ambiguous outcomes must not be blindly retried.
+5. Resolve the DigitalHandshake read-tool early return only if a real path can bypass explicit approval or legacy destructive intent. Keep this distinct from BaseAgent's ToolApprovalService path.
+
+Acceptance: unclassified callable cannot execute; known safe calls still work; denied/pending calls have no side effect; altered arguments require a new decision; concurrent approval cannot duplicate effects. Prove receipts and recovery per side-effecting adapter before promising exactly-once execution.
+
+## Unit 2 — TypeSafe answer contracts and conservative policy
+
+Files: `config/typesafeJudgments.ts`, its tests, `packages/firebase/src/functions/intelligence/typesafeClient.ts`, `typesafeJudge.ts`, and a small shared pure answer-contract module if reuse warrants it. Audit consumers under finance, agent guardrails/routing/memory, brand, catalog, distribution, video/image/audio/theme, and marketing. Include new flywheel/hillclimber/on-call consumers only after coordinating their ownership and intended inclusion.
+
+1. Define reusable parsers for actual API response shapes: Choice enum membership, finite probability/confidence ranges, Score bounds based on criterion count, and Noul in [0,1]. Reject null/boolean/numeric-string coercions; preserve missing, malformed, unavailable, and uncertain as distinct outcomes.
+2. Stop manufacturing confidence or affirmative tax guidance. Return unavailable/unknown through the established null/optional contract and preserve deterministic/user-entered evidence. Missing evidence must not become a negative factual assertion either.
+3. Preserve fractional Scores until a named domain policy explicitly maps them to bands. Retain confidence where behavior depends on certainty. Keep Choice/Score confidence distinct from Noul yes probability; if directional certainty is useful, label and compute it explicitly rather than presenting it as overall workflow confidence.
+4. Define per-consumer consequence-aware uncertainty/fallback policy. Do not impose one universal confidence threshold. Keep financial limits, authorization, publishing decisions, and verified blockers deterministic. Model output never grants permission.
+5. Remove redundant next-step Choice questions when code is intentionally authoritative, or consume them as advisory evidence with an explicit conflict policy. Do not let model suggestions override deterministic blockers.
+6. Complete transport timeout coverage through response/error-body reading, central size and serialization validation, explicit model precedence, resource cleanup, and bounded safe error messages. Preserve request ID and usage through relevant boundaries without logging private state.
+7. Separate credential rejection, timeout, rate limit, schema failure, and low confidence. Scope cooldowns to the affected capability/failure; avoid repeated paid shape failures and avoid suppressing unrelated healthy judgments. Surface real credential rejection through the official authorization path.
+8. Evaluate policy on representative consented/labeled cases: false affirmative rate for high-consequence actions, abstention/review rate, calibration, latency, fallback frequency, and token cost. Set thresholds from consequences and measurements rather than examples in docs.
+
+Acceptance: malformed answers never increase authority or confidence; midpoint Noul remains ambiguous; Scores retain fractional meaning; unknown Choice never silently selects a valid action; blocked deterministic conditions remain blocked at maximum model confidence. Slow body reads time out, oversized input is rejected before transport, and model selection is explicit. All consumers are inventoried, with each migrated, verified already-correct, or explicitly deferred with reason.
+
+Official contracts: https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice ; https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score ; https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul ; https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence ; https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/system-one . Current docs say Scores may be fractional and Noul has no separate confidence field.
+
+## Unit 3 — Shared interaction and accessibility contracts
+
+Files: `components/ui/Modal.tsx`, `hooks/useFocusTrap.ts`, callable Confirm/Alert/Prompt wrappers, `components/ui/button.tsx`, `tabs.tsx`, `FormField.tsx`, `progress.tsx`, and focused tests. Consult the react-call skill before changing callable dialog behavior.
+
+1. Make Escape work inside inputs and dismiss only the topmost eligible dialog. Respect existing close restrictions, consume the handled event, and restore focus to the correct connected trigger. Handle focus outside the trap and hidden/inert controls; assess background inertness and scroll locking for actual modal stacking.
+2. Use per-instance title/description IDs; give PromptDialog's input an accessible name. Preserve existing awaited return values and cancellation behavior.
+3. Define disabled/loading behavior for Slot children, including pointer and keyboard activation and child handler composition. Keep busy/spinner semantics truthful without breaking normal child callbacks.
+4. Compose Tabs callbacks with documented cancellation semantics; implement one roving tab stop. Preserve controlled/uncontrolled behavior and existing disabled-tab skipping. Add orientation support only if existing consumers require it.
+5. Merge FormField description IDs without duplicates; preserve caller validation unless the wrapper has an error. Clarify required-field behavior with actual callers before changing native constraint validation.
+6. Forward Progress value/max consistently to semantic root and visual calculation; define null/indeterminate and invalid-value handling.
+
+Acceptance: keyboard-only dialogs open/close and restore focus; one Escape affects one dialog; prompt is named; disabled/loading children cannot activate; callbacks do not accidentally break tab selection; one tab stop enters a tablist; descriptions and progress semantics match the rendered state. Verify representative finance/publishing/distribution dashboards and a callable prompt, not every caller by rote.
+
+## Unit 4 — Remaining UI, layout, loading, and motion review
+
+Inventory: textarea, badge, table, card/SectionCard, DropdownMenu, tooltip, slider, ScrollArea, Skeleton/DeptLoader, ThreeDButton/ThreeDCard, AgentIcon/feedback, shared layout/empty/error components, and specialized callable dialogs. Inspect representative callers and existing tests for each category. Leave already-correct components unchanged.
+
+Motion files: `components/motion-primitives/text-effect.tsx`, `animated-number.tsx`; global policy is already `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` in `core/AppShell.tsx:685`.
+
+1. Check motion in the actual app tree, including portal roots. Verify whether number springs, filters, stagger delays, and CSS animations honor the user's preference. Add local static/snap behavior only where the global policy does not achieve it.
+2. Ensure TextEffect has one coherent accessible text equivalent in word/char/line modes; verify changed text, multiline spacing, empty content, and Unicode segmentation. Check whether long streaming text causes excessive nodes or repeated animation before optimizing.
+3. Give AnimatedNumber a stable accessible value and sensible initial/update behavior. Validate finite values and supported precision at the public boundary; preserve intentional number animations where motion is allowed.
+4. Verify loading/status, empty/error/retry states, scroll-container keyboard use, small viewports, and nested interactive content in actual component uses. Use existing state components; add a new abstraction only after repeated missing behavior is demonstrated.
+5. Do not report Slider controlled values/min as broken: its final props spread already forwards them. Check scalar-versus-array public contract and actual callers before changing its API. Tabs already skip native disabled buttons; retain that behavior.
+
+Acceptance: no loss of content or function with reduced motion; semantic text and values are stable; keyboard users can reach overflowing content; actual loading/error states have understandable feedback and recovery. Browser evidence remains pending until genuine-account validation.
+
+## Unit 5 — Durable recovery and compaction
+
+Files to inspect: `services/agent/SessionService.ts`, `WorkflowStateService.ts`, `components/HistoryManager.ts`, `components/ContextPipeline.ts`, `BaseAgent.ts`, `governance/ToolApprovalService.ts`; backend `packages/firebase/src/functions/agent/workflowExecutionCallables.ts`, `workflowExecutionGraph.ts`, `executeWorkflowStep.ts`, `workflowOrchestrator.ts`, and their tests.
+
+1. Trace save/load/append/clear/delete and local persistence to their callers. Clarify cloud versus local success guarantees; inspect orphaned message cleanup and interrupted writes before proposing migration changes.
+2. Exercise backend claim fencing, resume/cancel, duplicate events, approval waits, and partial completion. Existing step execution rechecks its current claim before and after work; preserve it. A UUID alone is not side-effect idempotency.
+3. Verify the planner/generator/evaluator path and persisted verdicts. The inspected backend executor is explicitly text-only; documentation must not describe it as performing external actions.
+4. HistoryManager limits history to 25 messages before summarizing the older portion of that window. Trace older context into durable recall or an accumulated summary; define and repair loss only after confirming the full caller path. Preserve user constraints, pending approvals, identifiers, and actual tool receipts through compaction. A generated summary cannot confer permission.
+5. Record incomplete local saves and recovery outcomes honestly; do not replace unavailable persistence with silent successful empty history.
+
+Acceptance: real reload/resume retains intended state; cancelled/stale claims cannot commit; ambiguous side effects are reconciled rather than duplicated; constraints older than the active window remain available through the intended memory mechanism; summaries and transport compression are tested as separate mechanisms.
+
+## Unit 6 — Budgets, structured events, and audit evidence
+
+Files: `BaseAgent.ts`, `orchestration/AgentLoopService.ts`, `governance/TokenEstimator.ts`, `governance/AgentEventBus.ts`, `core/events.ts`, actual usage accounting and audit consumers, and backend `functions/security/logAuditEvent.ts` where needed.
+
+1. Define per-execution cumulative limits using actual provider usage plus a conservative preflight estimate and output reserve. Include retry/delegation usage and missing-usage behavior. Keep token, context-window, spend, credit, and user-approved overrides separate; do not silently disable one through another.
+2. Preserve typed timestamps, call/session/execution IDs, duration, failure reason, and approval outcome in events. Add a compatible typed channel or optional payload so existing AGENT_ACTION consumers continue working. Do not call a local event bus a remote stream without a real transport.
+3. Correlate audit decisions, claims, execution receipts, and failures with stable identities. Use redacted summaries or hashes rather than raw sensitive arguments. Choose awaited persistence or a durable outbox for mandatory records; document best-effort diagnostics separately.
+4. Verify immutability/ownership at the server and rules boundary before claiming immutable or hash-chained audit logs. Database edition discovery and security-rules auditor review are prerequisites if implementation changes Firestore models or rules.
+
+Acceptance: cumulative spend/tokens halt the next action correctly; retries do not reset budgets; event payloads survive subscribers; audit failure behavior is explicit; one call can be traced from request through decision to receipt without leaking secrets.
+
+## Coverage of all 12 harness primitives
+
+| Primitive | Current evidence | Planned disposition |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 1 Registry | Implementations and metadata are separate maps | Unit 1: complete inventory and consistency validation |
+| 2 Permissions | Known-tool approval gates exist; unknown custom-function gap | Unit 1: explicit classifications and dispatch enforcement |
+| 3 Persistence | Cloud sessions and local retry path exist | Unit 5: verify actual restore and failure semantics |
+| 4 Workflow state | Server callables and claim fencing exist | Unit 5: interruption, cancellation, duplicate/recovery checks |
+| 5 Token budgets | Estimator and static per-call ceiling exist | Unit 6: cumulative actual-usage accounting |
+| 6 Streaming events | Local typed shim flattens payload | Unit 6: preserve fields and verify delivery boundary |
+| 7 Event logging | Backend audit call is best-effort | Unit 6: correlation, durability, verified guarantees |
+| 8 Dual verification | Structural suites exist | Every unit: deterministic checks plus separate real-path evidence |
+| 9 Tool pools | Read-only/mode/module filters exist; soft cap | Unit 1: invariant tests; measure pools before changing caps |
+| 10 Compaction | Summarization/window and payload compression exist | Unit 5: evidence-preserving context and long-history checks |
+| 11 Permission audit | Pending approval records and decisions exist | Units 1/6: provenance, argument binding, receipts, failure recovery |
+| 12 Agent types | Domain configs/allowlists exist; generic roles unproven | Unit 1: verify allowed tools, delegation/spawn limits, turn caps by existing domain config; add only demonstrated missing enforcement |
+
+## Verification and delivery gates
+
+- Before each unit: confirm clean synchronized mainline and ownership of overlapping files; establish the baseline using the current code, not historical handoff claims.
+- Deterministic checks: narrow parser/domain-policy tests; component interaction/accessibility tests; actual dispatch/approval/budget invariants; existing related suites. Legacy mocks count only as structural evidence. Do not add simulated customer paths, credentials, persisted account history, or entitlements.
+- Commands after implementation: `npx vitest run <focused files>`, `node scripts/check-test-quality.js` (inspect supported file scoping), `npm run typecheck:renderer`, relevant Firebase/shared checks, and touched-file lint. Run required root checks for the final scope; builds can generate files, so inspect output before committing.
+- Real paths: read `.agent/REAL_USER_AUTHENTICITY.md`; use https://indii.music/ with genuine sign-in and existing account state, actual plan, and visible workflows. Record dialog keyboard/focus, dashboard tabs/progress, a real classification with uncertainty, and durable reload/resume. Never manufacture dangerous side effects for validation; use an existing legitimate approval request or remain unverified.
+- If credentials expire, stop that path and provide the official clickable authorization flow. Do not substitute another identity or token mechanism.
+- Verify exact pushed-SHA CI and report its URL/status. For docs-only work inspect Docs and Policy Gate. If no workflow is scheduled, state `Remote CI not scheduled for this path` and report local evidence.
+- Deployment is separate. If these fixes are not deployed, production behavior cannot validate the changed commit; leave deployed verification explicitly pending.
+- Update `docs/INDII_CONDUCTOR_HARNESS.md`, `docs/harness/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and TypeSafe guidance only to reflect implemented and observed guarantees. No blanket production-grade, immutable, cryptographic, or exactly-once assertions without corresponding evidence.
+

# Boardroom Context and Execution

Reviewed 2026-11-05. This chart describes the implementation; the [model migration chart](chat-model-routing-and-approval.md) separates current routing from the intended Argon architecture.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Workspace["Creative outputs and actionable releases"] --> Hook["useBoardroomContextHandshake: publish durable references"]
    Hook --> References["Referenced assets in shared store"]
    Prompt["Boardroom request and seated agents"] --> Snapshot["AgentService: snapshot request assets and session"]
    References --> Snapshot
    Snapshot --> Intent{"Conversation or action intent?"}
    Intent -->|Read-only or uncertain| Conversation["handleBoardroomSwarmFlow"]
    Conversation --> Greeting{"Trivial greeting?"}
    Greeting -->|Yes| Template["Local greeting without a model call"]
    Greeting -->|No| Discussion["Seated-agent conversation with read-only context"]
    Intent -->|Action| Route["Determine orchestration path and dependency steps"]
    Route --> Execute["Execute ready steps with original request and asset manifest"]
    Execute --> Approval["Tool policy and request-bound approval where required"]
    Approval --> Receipt["Per-step receipt from actual response and tool evidence"]
    Receipt --> Dependencies["Dependency results passed as evidence"]
    Dependencies --> Execute
    Receipt --> Final["Per-agent messages and Conductor receipt report"]
    Execute -->|Dispatch interrupted or rejected| Uncertain["Record uncertain outcome when dispatch started"]
    Uncertain --> Receipt
```

## Transition Breakdown

1. `useBoardroomContextHandshake.ts` publishes up to three recent supported creative outputs with durable references and up to two actionable releases. References supply context; they do not establish that an agent executed work.
2. `AgentService.handleBoardroomRequestFlow` snapshots uploads, references, gallery assets, and the active session. Image attachments retain their original pixels; the textual manifest uses aliases and elides base64 payloads.
3. Conversation and uncertain intent use a read-only dispatch. Trivial greetings can return a local template. A successful greeting therefore does not verify provider connectivity or tool execution.
4. Action routing builds single, parallel, or graph-derived steps. Each dispatched step receives the original request, source references, assigned owner, and dependency evidence. Tool approval remains a separate gate.
5. Each step produces a receipt; remaining steps can be skipped. The final Conductor response aggregates those receipts. An interrupted response after dispatch can leave an uncertain outcome requiring reconciliation.

## Diagnosis boundaries

The reported specialist-unavailable errors and repeated `report_bug` approval pauses affect the investigation of both direct chat and Boardroom. The reviewed code does not establish a general “summary protocol overwrites drafts” cause. Do not present that explanation or Department mode as a verified remedy. Asset retrieval, provider connectivity, approval continuation, and delivery rendering require separate checks.

Sources: `packages/renderer/src/hooks/useBoardroomContextHandshake.ts`, `packages/renderer/src/services/agent/AgentService.ts`, and its imported Boardroom receipt helpers. See [bug reporting and approval](08-bug-reporter-pipeline.md).

# Bug Reporting and Approval

Reviewed 2026-11-05. Agent-requested reporting has an approval gate before the reporting tool runs. A chat reply expressing consent currently does not establish that the pending approval was executed.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Agent["Agent requests report_bug"] --> Policy["BaseAgent tool policy"]
    Policy --> Pending["Persist pending approval with bound tool, arguments, user, and session"]
    Pending --> Pause["Return AWAITING_TOOL_APPROVAL and show Approvals panel"]
    Pause --> Choice{"User chooses exact pending request"}
    Choice -->|Deny| Denied["Record denied; do not execute"]
    Choice -->|Approve| Claim["ToolApprovalService: validate binding and claim execution"]
    Claim --> Tool["BugReportTools.report_bug validates required fields"]
    Tool --> Callable["Firebase callable reportBugFn"]
    Callable --> Auth["Require verified non-anonymous user and abuse protection"]
    Auth --> Hash["Server hashes title, module, severity, and description"]
    Hash --> Persist["Attempt Firestore bug_reports write"]
    Persist --> Token{"Server GitHub token available?"}
    Token -->|No| Skipped["GitHub skipped"]
    Token -->|Yes| Search["Search open issues by sanitized title phrase and module label"]
    Search --> Match{"Search returns a match?"}
    Match -->|Yes| Comment["Append duplicate-report comment to first match"]
    Match -->|No or search fails| Create["Attempt issue creation"]
    Comment --> Result["Return separate Firestore and GitHub statuses and issue URL if available"]
    Create --> Result
    Skipped --> Result
    Result --> Outcome["Record approval execution outcome and surface actual tool result"]
    Claim -->|Ambiguous dispatch failure| Reconcile["Keep claimed outcome unresolved for reconciliation"]
    Pause -.-> Consent["Conversational consent currently enters another model turn"]
    Consent -.-> Gap["Missing request-bound chat continuation: repair required"]
```

## Transition Breakdown

1. `BaseAgent.ts` binds the implementation, original arguments, schema, and execution context to a persisted approval request. It pauses without executing the tool.
2. `governance/ToolApprovalService.ts` approves a specific ID, validates the binding, and records a durable claim before dispatch. Denial does not execute the call. Ambiguous dispatch failures must not invite an automatic duplicate execution.
3. The current chat path lacks a request-bound natural-language approval continuation. Repeated “I approve” messages can produce another tool proposal and pause. A repair must identify the exact request and preserve its arguments and identity checks.
4. `BugReportTools.ts` calls **reportBugFn**, not a callable named reportBug. The server computes a truncated SHA256 key from title, module, severity, and description; the earlier chart incorrectly placed hashing in the client.
5. `reportBugFn.ts` attempts Firestore persistence before GitHub synchronization and reports channel statuses separately. GitHub credentials remain server-side. Authentication or abuse-protection rejection stops the callable before these writes.
6. GitHub deduplication is best effort: phrase search plus a module label, followed by the first match. Search errors fall back to creation. This is not an exact-title check, author restriction, or atomic guarantee against duplicate issues.

## Acceptance evidence still required

Verify approving and denying the same pending request in the real UI; ensure consent cannot authorize a different request; test interruption and duplicate clicks; confirm the original result returns to the conversation. Confirm a returned issue URL and persistence status before claiming a report was filed. An existing issue proves one report reached GitHub, not that every approval path works.
''')

cat > docs/billing/prepaid-introductory-pricing.md <<'EOF'
# First-term prepaid pricing

Policy confirmed 2026-11-12: retain the current monthly base prices. Quarterly,
six-month and annual prepayments receive approximately 15%, 30% and 50% off the
first prepaid term, respectively. Subsequent terms renew at the undiscounted
monthly base multiplied by the term length. Totals are rounded to whole USD
before tax; displayed monthly equivalents are approximate. Monthly subscriptions
and existing subscription contracts are unchanged.

| Tier | Monthly | First quarter → renewal | First six months → renewal | First year → renewal |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Start | $22 | $56 → $66 | $92 → $132 | $132 → $264 |
| Build | $55 | $140 → $165 | $231 → $330 | $330 → $660 |
| Scale | $110 | $281 → $330 | $462 → $660 | $660 → $1,320 |

Scale's first year equals Build's undiscounted annual price. The previously
mentioned $528 was based on the old discounted Build annual total; it is not the
new Scale charge. The founder subsequently authorized consistent math using the
current monthly base prices.

## Stripe configuration before release

Updating code does not change Stripe's catalog. Configure the following in the
same Stripe account and mode as the deployed checkout function:

1. Each `STRIPE_PRICE_{START|BUILD|SCALE}_{QUARTERLY|SIX_MONTH|ANNUAL}` must reference
   an active USD, licensed, per-unit recurring price for the **renewal** amount
   above, not the introductory amount. Use month intervals of 3/6/12 or a one-year
   interval for annual prices. Never mutate existing subscriptions to migrate
   their contracts as part of this change.
2. Each `STRIPE_COUPON_{TIER}_{PERIOD}_INTRO` must reference a valid USD
   **amount-off** coupon with `duration: once`, with the amount below in cents.
   If product-restricted, it must cover the recurring price's product.

| Tier | QUARTERLY | SIX_MONTH | ANNUAL |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| START | 1000 | 4000 | 13200 |
| BUILD | 2500 | 9900 | 33000 |
| SCALE | 4900 | 19800 | 66000 |

Checkout verifies the catalog against these amounts before creating a customer
or a payment session. Missing or stale configuration blocks checkout rather than
charging a different amount. Introductory coupons cannot be combined with
customer-entered promotion codes. The coupon applies to the first billed term
of a newly created prepaid subscription, including one that starts after a trial;
it does not discount later renewal invoices. This is a per-subscription offer,
not an account-lifetime redemption limit. Existing subscription changes continue
through their existing management path.

## Verification and release scope

- Public page: all cadence badges, first-term totals, approximate equivalents,
  renewal totals and tax/rounding disclosures.
- App and function pricing: matching introductory percentages, totals and regular
  renewal totals; legacy yearly alias carries the regular annual price.
- Checkout: reject mismatched price/currency/cadence and wrong or recurring coupons;
  apply the verified once-only coupon to the configured full-price recurring item.
- Structural tests cover those paths; they do not prove a live charge or renewal.
- Before enabling customer checkout, verify the real Stripe catalog, hosted
  checkout's first charge and renewal disclosure, and invoice behavior with an
  authorized genuine customer path. No purchase or deployment is authorized by
  this implementation record. Public beta checkout availability remains unchanged.
EOF

cat > docs/audits/loop-checkpoint-ownership-2026-11-13.md <<'EOF'
# Agent loop checkpoint ownership — 2026-11-13

## Problem and resulting behavior

A browser-local running set cannot coordinate two tabs/devices. Resume also trusted
its local execution cache, and all durable checkpoint saves were unconditional.
Two clients could therefore both proceed from an older READY checkpoint.

Every checkpoint save now uses a Firestore transaction comparing the exact
expected `checkpointRevision`. Creation requires a missing document and starts at
revision 1. Existing legacy documents without a revision can advance once from 0.
A deleted document cannot be silently recreated by a stale writer. Transaction
retries keep the original expected revision rather than claiming newer state.

Resume reads durable state before deciding what to do, validates the embedded
execution identity and checkpoint shape, and refuses a claimed/ambiguous dispatch.
Each action remains behind a required checkpoint save; the loser of a concurrent
claim never dispatches. Recorded action output remains eligible for evaluation
without repeating the action. Unknown outcomes still require reconciliation.

Database rules require the next consecutive safe-integer revision and the document
identity, in addition to the existing authenticated owner check. This rejects stale
unconditional writes from an older client as well as races between new clients.

## Compatibility and release

The change uses the existing STANDARD/native `(default)` database in
`indii-music-founder` (edition/access confirmed read-only). No production documents
were changed. The rule and client changes must be released together: after the new
rules are active, an older client cannot write an unversioned or stale checkpoint;
it stops before action dispatch rather than bypassing ownership. An interrupted
old DISPATCHING checkpoint still requires reconciliation. Do not reset its phase
to READY merely to make it resumable.

The scheduler's existing incomplete IDLE records are not made runnable by this
change. Scheduled-loop intake still needs valid definition, budget and action
checkpoint initialization, and remains a separate requirement.

## Verification

- 265 structural tests across 22 service/orchestration/governance files passed.
  Includes independent service instances racing for a revision, stale-cache
  resume, malformed checkpoint identities/phases, deleted records, legacy claims
  and transaction retries.
- All 370 tests in the Firestore security rules suite passed against an isolated
  STANDARD Firestore emulator on port 8189 using a demo project. Concurrent SDK
  transactions prove one claim succeeds and one is rejected; owner/cross-user,
  initial revision, skipped revision, stale write and legacy transitions are covered.
- These are structural/emulator results, not genuine-user production acceptance.
- The delivery report records final typecheck, lint and remote status.

## Rules audit

```json
{
  "score": 4,
  "summary": "The scoped revision/identity and owner guards pass the emulator suite. Full execution payload validation is still outside this change.",
  "findings": [{
    "check": "Storage abuse and payload shape",
    "severity": "minor",
    "issue": "Existing owner-writable loop history, definition and checkpoint payloads do not yet have comprehensive server-side shape/size limits.",
    "recommendation": "Add bounded execution schema and transition validation in the broader durable-execution work. Ownership derives from authenticated UID and path, never a submitted owner field."
  }]
}
```

## Remaining recovery requirements

This is not an exactly-once external-effect claim. Adapter-level idempotency keys,
durable side-effect receipts, reconciliation of ambiguous outcomes, mandatory
execution audit evidence, and acceptance through the deployed genuine-user path
remain open in the original primitives review. A bounded Jev check selected this
partial-completion interpretation; it did not certify source code or runtime behavior.

cat > docs/audits/scheduled-loop-admission-2026-11-13.md <<'EOF'
# Scheduled loop admission — 2026-11-13

## Reproduced defects

The old scheduler created IDLE executions at iteration 0 without a definition
snapshot, action checkpoint or saved token allowance, so the recovery service
could not safely resume them. It deduplicated by loop ID across tenants, preferred
a payload-selected owner over the user path, emitted ownerless root executions,
and generated a new random execution on each delivery. Discovery failures silently
fell back to root-only definitions. Eleven new regressions failed before repair.

## Resulting behavior

- Query all `SCHEDULE` definitions with the existing collection-group trigger index;
  the group query includes legacy root definitions. Discovery failure propagates.
- Validate source paths and owners. Scoped paths are authoritative; conflicting
  `userId` values are rejected. Root definitions require an explicit valid owner.
- Require a nonempty goal and criteria, valid iteration settings and the supported
  LLM evaluator. Unsupported deterministic evaluation is not queued.
- Create a stable execution ID from the full definition path and original scheduled
  occurrence. Native Firestore create-only writes preserve existing results/state
  on sequential or concurrent redelivery. Twenty writes run concurrently at most;
  a batch waits for all results before returning a partial failure for retry.
- Queue IDLE at iteration 1 with the exact definition snapshot, READY checkpoint,
  zero token spend, initial revision, source path and occurrence time. Canonical
  schema parsing preserves the scheduled provenance fields.
- Enable three bounded retries. Use UTC quarter-hour unix-cron syntax rather than
  the previous human-readable format: the latter omits the stable original-time
  header needed for retry deduplication. The SDK trigger metadata is tested.

Cloud Scheduler documents the original timestamp behavior and unix-cron
requirement in its [job schedule reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/scheduler/docs/configuring/cron-job-schedules)
and [deduplication guidance](https://docs.cloud.google.com/scheduler/docs/configuring/deduplicate-job-requests).

## Verification

- 60 tests across seven Firebase agent-function files passed, including 13
  scheduler unit regressions for initialization, tenant collisions, spoofed owners,
  legacy roots, duplicate/concurrent delivery, malformed definitions, discovery and
  write failure, partial retry, and delayed original-time delivery.
- Three isolated STANDARD Firestore emulator tests passed with the actual Admin SDK:
  native create-only concurrency, independent tenants and owned root definitions,
  retained completed results, distinct subsequent occurrences, invalid owners and
  real trigger metadata. Synthetic emulator data is structural evidence only.
- Full repository typecheck passed. Firebase source/test checking was repeated after
  the final trigger change. Changed-file lint, function deployment guards, test-quality
  scan, diff checks and flowchart validation passed.
- The actual packed shared artifact exports/loads the canonical loop schema using
  installed dependencies. The deployment workflow includes that built tarball;
  workspace-only symlinks are not a deployment package.
- Production data was not written and the function was not deployed.

## Scope and remaining work

This repairs queue admission, not autonomous scheduled action execution. No active
queue-to-agent worker is asserted: the repository currently exposes recovery
service APIs without a production consumer that drains this queue. Existing
incomplete/random-ID rows are not retrospectively rewritten or deleted because
current definitions cannot prove their original intent.

Deploy with the checkpoint-ownership client/rule changes when enabling recovery.
Production index readiness, real scheduler invocation, queue draining, genuine-user
acceptance, external-effect receipts and reconciliation remain required before
claiming a working autonomous scheduled-loop capability. The full primitives goal
remains open.
EOF

# Tool outcome audit reconciliation — 2026-11-13

Base: origin/main 5b1c29e7a. Delivery branch: codex/tool-audit-durability-20261113.

## Confirmed gap and change

BaseAgent's ordinary dispatch path returned credential-storage and non-retryable
failures before reaching its audit block. Other results scheduled an unawaited
write and could finish before the server acknowledged it. A logged rejection did
not provide a receipt or identify the event by its local invocation ID.

The dispatch path now awaits the existing authenticated logAuditEvent callable
before emitting/storing its completed tool result or taking terminal result
returns. The callable has a ten-second timeout. It continues to determine owner
identity on the server; the client does not submit a user ID in the payload.

Tool result metadata carries an explicit audit receipt: confirmed with the
server's document ID, unconfirmed after a rejection or malformed acknowledgement,
or unavailable when there is no user context. Tool success, error, data, failure,
and existing receipt metadata remain authoritative. A lost audit response is not
proof of a failed write. There is no automatic audit retry or repeated tool
execution. The audit links to the tool event with toolCallId and retains optional
agent fingerprint; arguments, generated assets, and raw tool errors are excluded.

## Scope still open

This fixes completion evidence in ordinary BaseAgent dispatch, not the full
mandatory-audit or external-effect recovery requirements:

- The approved-tool path in ToolApprovalService executes through a separate lane.
  Its durable claim and result state are not equivalent to a server audit receipt.
- A renderer can terminate after dispatch and before outcome persistence. A
  completion write cannot close that crash window or prove external-effect identity.
- Pre-dispatch durable intent/admission, cross-restart reconciliation and external
  provider idempotency remain necessary for mandatory evidence and safe recovery.
- No-user executions explicitly have no authenticated audit receipt.
- Audit metadata is retained in tool results; no new artist-facing audit-recovery
  control or persisted reconciliation queue is supplied by this change.
- Other execution lanes and direct tool/service calls require their own inventory
  and integration. No all-tools or exactly-once guarantee is made.

## Verification

Structural service tests hold acknowledgement pending, validate the returned log
ID, cover rejected/missing/malformed responses and synchronous setup failure, and
check status, identity linkage and absence of browser ownership. Orchestration
regressions hold terminal results until acknowledgement and preserve a successful
image receipt with an unconfirmed audit without repeating the tool.

The live Jev bounded policy check selected retaining the authoritative outcome
with audit uncertainty instead of rerunning the action or claiming an audit was
saved (jev-1.14.0; 466 input / 41 output tokens). This is design feedback, not code
certification or deployed-path evidence.

No production tool action or audit write was submitted. Structural tests do not
establish genuine-account acceptance, backend availability or deployed behavior.

# Conversation clear generations

Purpose: explain how conversation clearing coordinates message writes and
persistence retries across devices. Implemented locally and verified by structural
service/store tests and isolated STANDARD Firestore emulator rules tests. Genuine

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    C["Clear chat requested"] --> I["Store allocates one operation object and ID"]
    I --> B["Transaction reads session and binds starting generation"]
    B --> D{"Completed operation ID matches?"}
    D -->|Yes| Done["Return without querying or deleting messages"]
    D -->|No| G{"Starting generation still valid?"}
    G -->|No| Stop["Stop with conflict; no automatic retry"]
    G -->|Yes| F["Claim or resume operation; clear inline history"]
    F --> Q["Read at most 400 child messages from server"]
    Q --> T["Transaction verifies operation ID and generation"]
    T --> S{"Fence still belongs to this clear?"}
    S -->|No| Stop
    S -->|Yes| E{"Page empty?"}
    E -->|No| X["Delete the page in that transaction"]
    X --> Q
    E -->|Yes| R["Release fence and record completed operation ID"]
    R --> Done

    A["Append begins before upload"] --> Capture["Capture server generation; bind message object for retries"]

    Upload --> Check["Transaction checks active session and unchanged generation"]
    Check --> Valid{"Generation unchanged and no active clear?"}
    Valid -->|Yes| Save["Save child message with generation"]
    Valid -->|No| Stop
```

The parent session owns `messageEpoch`, `clearingOperation` and
`lastClearedOperation`. A distinct explicit clear may take over an interrupted
one by advancing the generation; every old worker verifies its ownership before
deleting. Automatic retries retain their original operation object and generation.
The completion receipt prevents a lost acknowledgement from clearing newly added
messages; generation binding rejects older retries after a newer clear.

Child writes use the post-write parent in security rules, so an atomic batch
cannot begin a clear and sneak an old-generation append through the same commit.
Generation zero supports legacy sessions. After a session has been cleared, old
clients that omit the generation fail closed and cannot restore inline history.
Client and rules changes require a coordinated release.

Source: `packages/renderer/src/services/agent/SessionService.ts`,
`packages/renderer/src/core/store/slices/agent/agentSessionSlice.ts`, and
`packages/firebase/firestore.rules`.

Remaining: uploaded objects can be orphaned when a clear invalidates an append;
this change does not delete attachment objects or prove cross-reload continuity of

# Conversation clear persistence — 2026-11-13

Base: origin/main 981d02397. Branch: codex/session-clear-generation-20261113.

## Reproduced gaps

Clear chat deleted one snapshot without a durable parent fence. Another device
could append during deletion. An attachment upload could start before a clear and
commit afterward. The store also retries failed persistence calls, so retrying an
acknowledged-but-response-lost clear with a fresh identity could delete messages
created after the first clear completed.

## Implemented protocol

- Each clear has one operation object/ID retained by the store across retries.
- The initial transaction binds its starting generation, advances messageEpoch,
  claims clearingOperation, and removes legacy inline history.
- A failed clear leaves the fence intact. The same operation resumes; a distinct
  explicit clear can take over with a new generation.
- Server-required queries drain pages of at most 400 messages. Each deletion
  transaction reads and verifies the parent operation/generation. A superseded
  worker cannot delete a page or release a newer fence.
- The final transaction releases the fence and records lastClearedOperation.
  A retry of that completed operation returns without deleting again. Generation
  binding also rejects an older retry after a newer clear replaces that receipt.
- Appends capture the server generation before uploading and bind the original
  message object across retries. Edits verify both parent and child generations.
- Generation/clear/delete conflicts stop automatic store retries and preserve the
  failed local message rather than resubmitting it as new work.

Rules validate bounded generation/operation fields on parent create and update,
prohibit generation rollback/skips, bind the completion receipt to its clear,
and prevent resurrecting inline history after the first clear. Child writes use
getAfter for same-batch parent changes and require the current active generation.
Owner authority remains pinned. Generation zero supports existing legacy sessions.

## Verification

The stale-append regression fails against the unchanged base implementation.
With the fix, 62 structural service/attachment/store tests across five files pass.
The STANDARD emulator suite passes all 371 rules tests, including cross-owner
writes, invalid/skipped/rolled-back generations, clearing-time writes, legacy
writes after clear, takeover transitions, and a same-batch fence/append race.
Renderer and Firebase-test typechecking, touched lint, whitespace, test-quality
and flowchart validation are final delivery gates.

Read-only CLI inspection reconfirmed the existing production `(default)` database
is STANDARD / FIRESTORE_NATIVE. No production data was changed. All writes in
rules verification target an isolated local emulator. These tests do not establish
a genuine-account save/clear journey or deployed behavior.

Jev selected stable, generation-bound retry identity rather than fresh deletion
on every retry (jev-1.14.0; 460 input / 40 output tokens). This is bounded policy
feedback, not correctness certification.

## Rules audit and remaining work

Scoped audit score: 4/5. Create/update authority, generation transitions, same-batch
post-state, completion identity and stale-client rejection were reviewed. The
inherited session/message payloads still lack complete bounded schemas; this
change validates the new protocol fields rather than claiming global rules
hardening. Owners can still intentionally delete their own data.

Client and rules require coordinated delivery. After a clear, old clients that
omit generations fail closed. The operation object survives current-process
retries, not renderer termination. New explicit clears can recover interrupted
fences; no unattended cross-restart recovery is claimed.

Attachment orphan inventory/cleanup, local-cache clear coherence, session-creation
acknowledgement recovery, execution-start generation binding for agent output
that has not yet begun persistence, complete schema validation and genuine
exact-deployed-commit acceptance remain open in the original primitives review.
EOF

calibration claim; the threshold needs labelled evaluation for each consumer.

playbook after an uncertain deterministic miss; VideoPopout can retain the raw
preview error; UpscalerService can retain its deterministic model selection.

judgment transports also require reconciliation; the original consumer inventory

budget guarantee is added by this branch.

and callers, authenticated authoritative admission before provider submission,
conservative handling of unknown usage, durable request/usage settlement receipts,

a mutable global current execution would mix concurrent conversations. Provider
limits and pricing must be verified before selecting reservation amounts rather

callers must then be inventoried and exercised, including concurrent/recovered
runs. These are outstanding implementation requirements, not completed design.

# Ambient creative evidence contracts — 2026-11-13

Base: origin/main 981d02397. Branch: codex/ambient-creative-evidence-20261113.

## Reproduced evidence gaps

Creative mode, gallery prompt-to-brand scoring and campaign format selection
replaced absent/invalid provider confidence with numeric heuristic confidence.
Their deterministic fallbacks also invented confidence values. The mode banner
called this a match percentage, and campaign tags called it percent fit. Gallery
badges described asset fit even though only prompt text and brand context were
submitted. Campaign slots zero through two were automatically awarded Top Pick
before any output comparison. Prompt words such as glitch were interpreted as
rendered defects and recommended retry despite no output inspection.

## Implemented changes

All three verdicts now distinguish source=heuristic with null confidence from an
adopted typed provider result with source=jev and actual bounded confidence.
Mode adopts Choice confidence at least 0.70; gallery Score and campaign Choice
adopt confidence at least 0.65. These are adoption policies, not calibration.
Invalid, missing, coerced, low-confidence or wrong-type responses preserve the
existing deterministic suggestion. Gallery scores still require the declared
0–4 provider range before mapping to the displayed 1–5 scale.

Heuristic mode guidance stays available as a prompt keyword suggestion without a
percentage, preserving the user's Switch control. Cinematic styling and camera
equipment words alone no longer imply video; camera movement still can. Gallery
labels and accessible names identify prompt-to-brand matching and its source,
without asserting pixel inspection. Campaign tags describe layout and distinguish
format heuristics from Jev confidence. Hero/thumbnail labels no longer imply
measured conversion or safety. Slot-position Top Pick awards were removed.

Prompt wording alone cannot establish an output defect or justify a paid retry.
Actual failed-slot retry controls, playable-result requirements and launch guards
are preserved. Format classification does not launch or retry a campaign.

## Verification and limits

All 12 initial evidence regressions fail on base. Parser/service and UI checks
cover actual provider confidence, heuristic guidance without fake percentages,
source-aware campaign tags, absence of unearned awards, and static-camera versus
camera-motion routing. The final selected suite covers central judgments, direct
generation controls, campaign status and gallery rendering/accessibility/
interactions. These structural tests use simulated service boundaries and do not
establish a genuine account, generation, inspection or production journey.

One direct live Jev fixture chose image mode for a cinematic watercolor static
album-cover prompt (jev-1.14.0; 397 input / 40 output tokens). It is a semantic
smoke check, not calibration, proxy acceptance or model-training evidence.

Other judgments and deterministic patterns still need calibration and consumer
review. Actual image/video quality verification, cumulative semantic/monetary
budgets, durable effect recovery and exact-deployed genuine-account acceptance
remain open in the original primitives objective. No merge or deployment is
performed by this branch.

Base: origin/main 711f66b95. Branch: codex/memory-write-receipts-20261113.

## Reproduced failures

MemoryBankService swallowed rejected writes as empty arrays, and index_memory

## Implemented contract

- AlwaysOnMemoryEngine exposes a structured stored/skipped/unconfirmed receipt.
  Stored requires a primary persisted memory ID and an unchanged active owner.
  Legacy text presentation delegates to the receipt path for compatibility.
- File ingestion and session extraction also require IDs before claiming/counting
  new saves. Activity accounting tracks overlapping ingestions by owner generation;
  an older owner's completion cannot clear the new owner's activity state.
- Semantic indexing validates nonempty record IDs/content and propagates rejected
  or incomplete acknowledgements. Aggregate search behavior retains the separate
  successful-empty versus unavailable distinction.
- The three explicit save tools claim success only with a stored ID. Skips use
  MEMORY_NOT_SAVED; uncertain responses use MEMORY_SAVE_UNCONFIRMED. BaseAgent
  stops either outcome using its actual agent identity instead of prompting an
  automatic repeated write. Unauthenticated indexing stops before dispatch.

The 119-test selected run spans 12 memory, tool and BaseAgent suites. It covers

p.write_text('''---
description: Inspected text-model routing, the Argon/Flash intelligence target, and specialty, media, approval, and verification boundaries.
---

# Chat Model Routing and Intelligence Hierarchy

Reviewed against source on 2026-11-13. This chart distinguishes configured routing
from the founder's required hierarchy: Argon directs the Conductor, Flash 3.8
provides other agents' intelligence, and trained models perform matching specialty
tasks. Preserve the trained models, their identities, prompts, and tool boundaries.
Source inspection does not establish active Remote Config values, provider access,
or genuine deployed behavior.

## Inspected routing

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Chat["Direct chat or Boardroom agent request"] --> Identity["Agent identity, prompt, tools, and context"]
    Identity --> Select{"BaseAgent config supplies modelId?"}
    Select -->|Yes| Explicit["Use configured model ID"]
    Select -->|No| Registry["Strict getFineTunedModel registry"]
    Nucleus["IndiiNucleus generalist selection"] --> Registry
    Registry --> Tuned["Reviewed R8 endpoint or explicit domain alias"]
    Explicit --> Resolve["Firebase client resolves recognized keys and Remote Config overrides"]
    Tuned --> Resolve
    Resolve --> Gateway["generateContentStream backend"]
    Gateway --> Admission["Verified auth, App Check, cost admission, model allowlist"]
    Admission --> Kind{"Approved model is a tuned endpoint?"}
    Kind -->|Yes| Vertex["Resolve full endpoint project and location"]
    Kind -->|No| Base["Use approved base model"]
    Vertex --> Response["Stream response or explicit failure"]
    Base --> Response
    Vertex -->|Unavailable or disabled| Failure["Specialist-unavailable result; no general-model substitution"]
    Identity --> Tools["Independent tool authorization, approval, and result evidence"]
    Tools --> Media["Image, video, audio, retrieval, and department capabilities"]
```

## Configured model references

These are repository values, not a claim that a provider currently accepts every
ID or that each agent invokes it in production.

| Source and role | Configured reference | Routing implication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Renderer `TEXT_AGENT` | `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` | Current client default for recognized agent capability keys; a Remote Config override can replace it. This literal is absent from the inspected server text-stream allowlist. |
| Renderer `TEXT_FAST` | `gemini-3.8-flash` | Configured workhorse reference, present in the server allowlist. |
| Server `TEXT.PRO` | `gemini-4-argon` | Server default when the stream request omits a model; present in the allowlist. It does not rewrite a supplied tuned endpoint. |
| Server `TEXT.FAST` | `gemini-3.8-flash` | Configured server workhorse reference. |
| Agent registry | Generated Vertex endpoint resource IDs and domain aliases | Default BaseAgent selection remains trained routing unless a model ID is supplied explicitly. Missing/disabled tuned routing fails visibly. |
| Fast and Pro images | `gemini-3.1-flash-image`, `gemini-3-pro-image` | Separate image paths; text routing changes do not prove image capability. |
| Server legacy image path | `gemini-2.5-flash-image` | Retained legacy image reference; validate its supported path separately. |

## Required intelligence hierarchy

Dashed edges describe the target and its acceptance work, not deployed-state proof.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    User["User goal and constraints"] -.-> Conductor["Argon Conductor plans and coordinates"]
    Conductor -.-> Intelligence["Flash 3.8 department intelligence"]
    Intelligence -.-> Scope{"Task matches a trained specialty?"}
    Scope -.->|Yes| Worker["Matching trained model handles bounded specialty task"]
    Scope -.->|No| Reroute["Keep in intelligence layer or select another qualified specialty"]
    Worker -.-> Evidence["Return result, provenance, and tool evidence"]
    Evidence -.-> Intelligence
    Reroute -.-> Intelligence
    Intelligence -.-> Review["Conductor checks goal and evidence"]
    Review -.-> Deliver["Deliver verified outcomes and explicit uncertainty"]
```

## Transition Breakdown

1. [BaseAgent](../../packages/renderer/src/services/agent/BaseAgent.ts) gives an
   explicit `config.modelId` precedence; otherwise it calls the strict
   [trained-model registry](../../packages/renderer/src/services/agent/fine-tuned-models.ts).
   [IndiiNucleus](../../packages/renderer/src/services/agent/IndiiNucleus.ts) also
   explicitly selects the generalist tuned endpoint. Changing one model label
   cannot by itself establish the required hierarchy.
2. The [Firebase intelligence client](../../packages/renderer/src/services/intelligence/FirebaseIntelligenceService.ts)
   resolves recognized capability/model keys and optional Remote Config overrides.
   An unrecognized full endpoint ID is preserved. Active cloud overrides have not
   been inspected for this chart.
3. The [stream gateway](../../packages/firebase/src/index.ts) checks the
   [server-owned allowlist](../../packages/firebase/src/config/textStreamModels.ts),
   validates reservation coverage, and resolves approved tuned endpoint resources.
   A disabled or unavailable specialist produces a typed failure; it is not
   silently replaced with a general model. A public error alone does not identify
   the original provider/routing cause.
4. Compare [renderer model configuration](../../packages/renderer/src/core/config/intelligence-models.ts)
   with [server configuration](../../packages/firebase/src/config/models.ts).
   The client/server agent-default mismatch above needs resolution and exact-path
   verification; configured Argon availability does not prove Conductor dispatch.
5. Trained specialty dispatch, out-of-scope rerouting, and handoff remain separate
   acceptance requirements. Preserve the agents' specialized prompts and tools.
   Media models and capabilities retain their independent provider and admission
   paths, including fast, Pro, and legacy image references where supported.
6. Keep approvals request-bound and deterministic. See [approval lifecycle](08-bug-reporter-pipeline.md),
   [Boardroom execution](04-boardroom-context-orchestration.md), and
   [stream reservation lifecycle](agent-stream-reservation-boardroom-budget.md).
   Provider response, consent, tool execution, persisted receipt, and visible
   deliverable are distinct facts.

## Completion criteria

- Align actual Conductor and department dispatch with approved provider IDs and
  admission rules; retain trained models for matching specialty tasks.
- Verify specialty scope, out-of-scope rerouting, and result/evidence handoff.
- Exercise genuine authenticated direct chat and Boardroom paths, including
  request-bound approve/deny, interruption, and recovery.
- Verify fast and Pro image generation, retained supported legacy/media paths,
  and asset retrieval independently of text generation.
- Inspect exact-commit CI and genuine deployed results before declaring the
  migration complete. Source labels, an allowed ID, and local tests are partial
  evidence only.
''')

content.text:
Yes—two new models are worth evaluating:

| Current role | Candidate | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Flash 3.8 department intelligence | **Gemini 4 Hydrogen** | Built for fast agentic work, tool use, and multimodal tasks. |
| Argon Conductor | **Gemini 4 Carbon** | Stronger deep reasoning, with more thinking time and potentially higher total token spend. |

Google documents these roles in its [current model comparison](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/latest-model) and [Carbon migration guide](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/whats-new-gemini-4-carbon).

My recommendation is to benchmark **Hydrogen for departments and Carbon for demanding Conductor work**, retaining Argon as an explicit faster option. Keep our trained specialists and image-generation tools.

The API update worth investigating is **Interactions API**: optional server-side conversation state, observable execution steps, and background jobs—relevant to our long conversations and agent workflows. [Official documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/capabilities/interactions)

Our integration needs preparation: the SDK is locked at **2.12.0**, and allowlists, thinking options, context budgets, and pricing need updating. New automatic-continuation features require newer SDK versions. [Migration requirements](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/start/get-started-with-gemini-4)

No runtime models have been switched yet.

## Final-response guardrail accounting

`BaseAgent` passes its active execution ledger to `JevGuardrailService`. Screening
reserves the remaining allowance before invoking `typesafeJudge`, and complete
usage receipts settle the ledger before the returned probabilities are read.
Exhausted allowance skips this optional judgment. Missing or malformed usage and
